dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:1401.text: That which the feet tread upon. Formed from 足, with 叚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1402.text: Amputation of a foot, 跀. Formed from 足, with 非 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 匪.

shuowen:1403.text: To cut off a foot. Formed from 足, with 月 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1404.text: A horse with bent shanks. Formed from 足, with 方 indicating the sound. Pronounced the same as 彭.

shuowen:1405.text: A horse's gait. Formed from 足, with abbreviated 決 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1406.text: An animal's foot raised on tiptoe. Formed from 足, with 幵 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1407.text: A road. Formed from 足 and 各.

shuowen:1408.text: To crush by treading. Formed from 足, with 㷠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1409.text: A foot with extra toes. Formed from 足, with 支 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1410.text: 蹁蹮: to move in a turning course. Formed from 足, with 䙴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1411.text: 蹭蹬: to lose one's way. Formed from 足, with 曾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1412.text: The loss of one's way called 蹭蹬. Formed from 足, with 登 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1413.text: 蹉跎: to miss the proper time. Formed from 足, with 差 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1414.text: The missing of one's time called 蹉跎. Formed from 足, with 它 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1415.text: To press upon. Formed from 足, with 戚 indicating the sound. Your servants Xu Xuan and others note: Li Shan's commentary on the Selections of Literature uses it interchangeably with 蹴.

shuowen:1416.text: 踸踔: the appearance of an irregular gait. Formed from 足, with 甚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1417.text: A foot. The upper part depicts the calf; the lower part is 止. The Duties of Disciples says: “Ask where the 疋 rests.” Ancient writing uses it for the 疋 of the Odes' Greater Elegantiae and also for 足. Some say it is 胥. Another explanation: 疋 means to record. All characters in the 疋 category are formed from 疋.

shuowen:1418.text: An open lattice window in a doorway. Formed from 疋; 疋 also indicates the sound. 囪 depicts its form. Pronounced like 疏.

shuowen:1419.text: To pass through. Formed from 爻 and 疋; 疋 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:1420.text: The multitude. Formed from three 口. All characters in the 品 category are formed from 品.

shuowen:1421.text: Much speech. Formed from interconnected 品. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “They encamped north of Nie.” Pronounced the same as 聶.

shuowen:1422.text: Birds calling in a flock. Formed from 品 above 木.

shuowen:1423.text: A bamboo musical pipe with three holes, used to harmonize the many sounds. Formed from 品 and 侖; 侖 means order. All characters in the 龠 category are formed from 龠.

shuowen:1424.text: 䶴 is the music of tuned pipes and clay ocarinas. Formed from 龠, with 炊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1425.text: Pipe music. Formed from 龠, with 虒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1426.text: To harmonize. Formed from 龠, with 禾 indicating the sound. Pronounced the same as 和.

shuowen:1427.text: Musical harmony. Formed from 龠, with 皆 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: “The eight kinds of instruments can harmonize.”

shuowen:1428.text: A document of investiture, which feudal lords advance to receive from the king. It depicts slips alternately long and short, with two binding cords through the middle. All characters in the 冊 category are formed from 冊.

shuowen:1429.text: A feudal lord succeeding to a state. Formed from 冊 and 口, with 司 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1430.text: An inscription. Formed from 戶 and 冊; 戶冊 is writing inscribed on a doorway.

shuowen:1431.text: Many mouths. Formed from four 口. All characters in the 㗊 category are formed from 㗊. Pronounced like 戢; also like 呶.

shuowen:1432.text: The sound of speech. Formed from 㗊, with 臣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1433.text: Sound, with breath emerging above the head. Formed from 㗊 and 頁; 頁 is the head.

shuowen:1434.text: A loud voice. Another explanation: a great shout. Formed from 㗊, with 丩 indicating the sound. The Gongyang Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Duke Zhao of Lu cried out loudly.”

shuowen:1435.text: To call out. Formed from 㗊, with 萈 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 讙.

shuowen:1436.text: Vessels. It depicts the mouths of vessels, with 犬 guarding them.

shuowen:1437.text: That within the mouth used to speak and distinguish flavors. Formed from 干 and 口; 干 also indicates the sound. All characters in the 舌 category are formed from 舌.

shuowen:1438.text: To drink. Formed from 舌, with 沓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1439.text: To take food with the tongue. Formed from 舌, with 易 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1440.text: To intrude or offend. Formed from reversed 入 and 一. All characters in the 干 category are formed from 干.

shuowen:1441.text: To push or reach, 㨖. Formed from 干. 入 with one line makes 干; 入 with two makes 𢆉. Pronounced like 能. It expresses a somewhat greater degree.

shuowen:1442.text: Not compliant. Formed from 干 with 屮 below, reversing it.

shuowen:1443.text: The upper arch of the mouth. Formed from 口, with the upper part depicting its texture. All characters in the 𧮫 category are formed from 𧮫.

shuowen:1444.text: The appearance of a tongue. Formed from abbreviated 𧮫; a pictograph.

shuowen:1445.text: A particle ending an utterance. Formed from 口, depicting breath drawn downward. All characters in the 只 category are formed from 只.

shuowen:1446.text: Sound. Formed from 只, with 甹 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 聲.

shuowen:1447.text: Halting speech. Formed from 口 and 内. All characters in the 㕯 category are formed from 㕯.

shuowen:1448.text: To pierce something with an awl. Formed from 矛 and 㕯. Another explanation: something emerging from fullness.

shuowen:1449.text: To know the inside from the outside. Formed from 㕯, with abbreviated 章 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1450.text: Curved. Formed from 口, with 丩 indicating the sound. All characters in the 句 category are formed from 句.

shuowen:1451.text: To restrain. Formed from 句 and 手; 句 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:1452.text: A fish trap made of bent bamboo. Formed from 竹 and 句; 句 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:1453.text: Curved. Formed from 金 and 句; 句 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:1454.text: To intertwine. Another explanation: melons and gourds forming curling tendrils. A pictograph. All characters in the 丩 category are formed from 丩.

shuowen:1455.text: Plants intertwining. Formed from 茻 and 丩; 丩 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:1456.text: Three strands of rope united. Formed from 糸 and 丩.

shuowen:1457.text: Old or former. Formed from 十 and 口: remembering earlier words. All characters in the 古 category are formed from 古.

shuowen:1458.text: Great and far-reaching. Formed from 古, with 叚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1459.text: The completeness of numbers. 一 represents east and west; | represents south and north, thus the four directions and center are complete. All characters in the 十 category are formed from 十.

shuowen:1460.text: Ten feet. Formed from 又 holding 十.

shuowen:1461.text: Ten hundreds. Formed from 十 and 人.

shuowen:1462.text: Resonance spreading. Formed from 十 and 䏌.

shuowen:1463.text: 卙卙: abundant. Formed from 十 and 甚. In Runan, abundance of silkworms is called 卙.

shuowen:1464.text: Broadly comprehensive. Formed from 十 and 尃; 尃 means to spread.

shuowen:1465.text: The ability of ten people. Formed from 十, with 力 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1466.text: Two tens combined. An abbreviated ancient form.

shuowen:1467.text: Speech described as 𠦫. Formed from 十, with 咠 indicating the sound. [The source supplies no further explanation of the descriptive word.]

shuowen:1468.text: Three tens combined. An abbreviated ancient form. All characters in the 卅 category are formed from 卅.

shuowen:1469.text: Thirty years make one 丗. Formed from 卅 extended with a trailing stroke; its sound is also taken from 卅.

shuowen:1470.text: Direct speaking is called 言; discussion and debate are called 語. Formed from 口, with 䇂 indicating the sound. All characters in the 言 category are formed from 言.

shuowen:1471.text: Sound. Formed from 言, with 賏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1472.text: To cough. Formed from 言, with 殸 indicating the sound. 殸 is the large-seal form of 磬.

shuowen:1473.text: To discuss. Formed from 言, with 吾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1474.text: To speak. Formed from 言, with 炎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1475.text: To report or reply. Formed from 言, with 胃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1476.text: Trustworthiness. Formed from 言, with 京 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1477.text: To convey words. Formed from 言 and 先; 先 also indicates the sound. The Odes says: “The locust wings, thronging together.”

shuowen:1478.text: To request an audience. Formed from 言, with 青 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1479.text: To report. Formed from 言, with 曷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1480.text: To heed or permit. Formed from 言, with 午 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1481.text: To answer, 𧭭. Formed from 言, with 若 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1482.text: To answer in words. Formed from 言, with 𨿳 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1483.text: Like 𧭭, to respond. Formed from 言, with 雔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1484.text: To distinguish or argue. Formed from 言, with 者 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1485.text: Intent or aspiration. Formed from 言, with 寺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1486.text: A fulfilled prediction. Formed from 言, with 韱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1487.text: To recite. Formed from 言, with 風 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1488.text: To recite. Formed from 言, with 甬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1489.text: To recite a book. Formed from 言, with 賣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1490.text: Pleasant or quick. Formed from 言 and 中.

shuowen:1491.text: To explain and instruct. Formed from 言, with 川 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1492.text: To enlighten and teach. Formed from 言, with 每 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1493.text: To teach exclusively or intently. Formed from 言, with 巽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1494.text: To illustrate or explain. Formed from 言, with 辟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1495.text: To speak gently. Formed from 言, with 原 indicating the sound. The Mencius says: “Thus he comes speaking gently and earnestly.”

shuowen:1496.text: To know early. Formed from 言, with 央 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1497.text: To inform. Formed from 言, with 俞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1498.text: To debate. Ancient writing uses it for 頗. Formed from 言, with 皮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1499.text: To inform and explain thoroughly. Formed from 言, with 𦎫 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 庉.

shuowen:1500.text: Earnest, repeated speech, 諄謘. Formed from 言, with 屖 indicating the sound.
